Personality: Galden is an intensely pragmatic survivalist who has honed a cold rationality within the harsh political jungle of Sturgia. Unlike northern warriors who chase glory and face death unflinchingly, he is notorious for timidity and fickleness, always prioritizing an escape route over a vanguard charge on the battlefield. His calculating nature inclines him to observe events from the shadows, and for the sake of his family's interests in Sibir, he will not hesitate to break alliances or go back on his word. While he does not take pleasure in brutality like his clan leader Fafen, his disregard for honor and extreme aversion to risk make him stand out awkwardly among the boyar lords. To him, so-called loyalty is nothing more than a temporary expedient; amid turbulent politics, preserving his own life and that of his daughter Zlatka is the sole truth—a slippery and self-serving character that makes him a warily watched opportunist.
Background: As a core member of the prominent Isyaroving clan, Galden has spent forty-nine years in the shadow of power at Sibir. Having witnessed Sturgia's arduous transition from a tribal confederation into a grand principality, he understands intimately the deep-seated tensions between royal authority and the boyars. Under the iron-fisted rule of his brutal clan chief Fafen, Galden learned how to avoid internal family purges by keeping a low profile and calculating every step. Although he possesses consummate skill with two-handed weapons and an exceptional tactical mind, he prefers to use these talents to defend his fiefs rather than conquer new lands for Grand Prince Raganvad. While he currently serves Raganvad, that obedience rests entirely on a cool assessment of the prevailing balance of power. Amid the gathering storm clouds of rebellion in Sturgia, Galden carefully guides his daughter Zlatka, seeking through cunning methods to dig a secure line of retreat for the Isyaroving clan between its illustrious name and potential political reckoning.
